opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Ads and customer acquisition — the company's biggest single expense line, 28% of revenue. Up only 7%, so marketing was not the margin problem this quarter.

opex.name: Operations and support
opex.note: Fulfillment, customer care and the care teams behind the platform. Up 39% as the subscriber base and international footprint grew.

opex.name: Technology and development
opex.note: The product and engineering teams, including the AI-native experience management keeps talking about. Up 71% — the fastest-growing opex line.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Offices, legal, finance and executive costs. Up 88% — nearly doubled, the biggest absolute jump in opex (+$70.8M), reflecting acquisition integration and the cost of running a much bigger, more global company.

follow100Note: The striking thing: the company spends $27.77 of every $100 on marketing and another $17.01 on G&A — together more than the entire gross profit left after product costs. A year ago, cost of revenue took only ~$26 of every $100; now it takes ~$43, and that 17-point margin collapse is what turned a profitable quarter into a loss.
footerNote: Chart note: Hims & Hers' running costs exceeded its gross profit, so the chart draws the $33.040M net loss as a 'Covered by cash on hand' source that funds the operating gap — the shortfall came from the balance sheet, not from revenue. The $13.210M tax benefit is drawn as its own green source.
oneTimers: Restructuring charges ($3.8M in Q3; $41.9M in the first nine months): costs from the February 2026 strategic shift in the U.S. weight-loss offering — moving to branded GLP-1 drugs and offering compounded GLP-1s only on a limited scale. The company adds these back in Adjusted EBITDA.

Acquisition, transaction and investment earn-out costs ($35.4M in Q3; $77.6M in nine months): deal costs and earn-outs tied to the international acquisitions behind the rest-of-world surge. Also added back in Adjusted EBITDA.
Legal contingencies ($62.5M in the first nine months, $0 in Q3): booked earlier in 2026, not in this quarter's numbers — but it is why the nine-month net loss (−$211.4M) is far worse than Q3 alone.
Stock-based compensation ($64.5M in Q3; $143.5M in nine months): a real, recurring cost of paying employees in shares — excluded from Adjusted EBITDA, but it dilutes shareholders.

Adjusted vs GAAP gap: Adjusted EBITDA of $82.4M vs a GAAP net loss of −$33.0M. The bridge is mostly stock comp ($64.5M), acquisition costs ($35.4M), depreciation ($38.2M) and the tax benefit. Adjusted net income is only $6.5M — even on management's preferred basis, the quarter was barely profitable.
otherDetail: A $21.112M paper gain on equity securities, plus a $3.821M gain on liabilities, less $5.037M of other expense — net $19.896M.

segments.name: United States
segments.note: The home market: subscription sales of prescription and non-prescription health products plus medical consultations. Still 74% of revenue, but growing slower (+21%) than the total.

segments.name: Rest of world
segments.note: International sales more than quadrupled (+321%) — the big growth story this quarter, driven by the company's international expansion and acquisitions. Now 26% of revenue, up from 9% a year ago.

takeaways.text: Revenue +49% with international sales up 321% — but that growth came with acquisitions, a much higher cost base, and a gross margin down 17 points. This is no longer the high-margin U.S. subscription story of a year ago.
takeaways.title: The growth is real, but it changed shape

takeaways.text: Subscribers grew 13% to 2.79M and each subscriber now pays $105/month (up 30%). Demand is healthy — the problem is that opex grew $145M while gross profit grew only $67M, with G&A nearly doubling.
takeaways.title: The loss is a spending story, not a demand story

takeaways.text: Full-year revenue was tightened to $3.13–3.15B while Adjusted EBITDA guidance was reduced to $257–277M. Management is spending ahead of Q4 platform expansions it says will set up 2027 — investors have to take on trust that the spending pays off.
takeaways.title: Guidance got more cautious on profit, not on sales

verdict: Revenue jumped 49% as international sales more than quadrupled, but Hims & Hers swung to a $33 million loss as gross margin collapsed 17 points and spending on marketing, admin and acquisitions piled up — growth bought at the cost of profitability.
